summary: Successfully cancelled the Streamly+ subscription. Confirmation code: HC-2481-ESCAPED. The account retains access until Sep 14 with no further billing. Throughout the cancellation flow, I documented 9 distinct dark patterns: hidden_path (cancel link buried in footer's "Membership settings"), two retention_offers (pause/downgrade and 50% discount), forced_survey (mandatory reason selection), fake_urgency (countdown timer on discount offer), guilt_trip (emotional appeal about losing watchlist/shows), confirmshaming ("Yes, take it all away from me"), misdirection (keep button visually dominant), artificial_delay (fake "specialist reviewing account" spinner), price_hike_threat (grandfathered $15.99 vs $22.99 warning), and repeated_confirmation (multiple are-you-sure screens).

patterns.evidence: The cancel option is buried under a footer link "Membership settings", and on that page the cancellation link "continue to membership cancellation" is at the very bottom, after retention offers.
"Pause your membership for up to 3 months. Keep your profile, watchlist, and grandfathered price." and "Standard with ads is only $6.99 a month." are interposed before the cancel option.
"We can't continue until you tell us why you're thinking of leaving." - must select a reason to proceed.
"50% off for 3 months - Keep everything you love for just $7.99 a month."
"This one-time offer expires in 4:57." - countdown timer to pressure user.
"You're 2 episodes from finishing Moonrise Protocol. Your 4 saved shows, your viewing history, and your personalized picks will all be gone."
"Yes, take it all away from me" - the cancel button is worded to shame the user.
"No, keep the things I love" is the visually dominant option vs "Yes, take it all away from me" for cancellation.
"Connecting you to a cancellation specialist - Please stay on this page. A specialist is reviewing your account..."
"You are on a grandfathered plan at $15.99. If you cancel, this price is gone forever. New members pay $22.99 for the same plan."
"Are you absolutely sure?" - This is yet another are-you-sure screen after the guilt trip page already asked the same question.
